clues: This port town sits on an island off the coast of Brazil, in a rich state in the south east. The same island holds one more town too.
This town sits just past the tropics, yet rain falls all year with no dry time. That kind of wet, warm air is most often found near the equator.
A Portuguese lord named Brás Cubas founded this town in 1546. He set it up as a new port for ships from across the sea.
The garden by this beach is the largest of its kind in the whole world. It runs a long way along the sand, past the waves.
In the old coffee museum here, world coffee prices were once agreed. Ships still move a huge share of the trade of Brazil through its port.
